news.title: WSL Highlights: Charlton Athletic 0-6 Chelsea
Rogers: I want to be more ruthless in front of goal
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers is determined to become more clinical in front of goal, with the Chelsea forward keen to build on his superb solo effort in our 2-0 Premier League victory over Manchester United. The England international broke the deadlock early in the second half at Stamford Bridge, producing a brilliant individual goal to help the Blues return to winning ways. But despite having scored six goals and provided four assists in all competitions this term, Rogers believes there is still plenty of room for improvement in his attacking game. Rogers said: 'I think being more clinical in front of goal, being more ruthless in and around the box, is something that previously I was a bit disappointed in myself because I'd score a nice goal every once in a while, but I wouldn't score the easy goals. I'm trying to work on that here. 'I'm trying to improve in my final actions, so that's my biggest one. I'm an attacker, so I try to score goals and assist and create chances, and I want to keep improving. I'm not there yet, but it's a good start!' Rogers certainly demonstrated his quality for the opener, collecting Romeo Lavia's pass in midfield before driving towards the visitors' penalty area. With Estevao making a supporting run, the 24-year-old spotted an opening in the United defence, glided beyond two challenges and calmly dinked the ball over Senne Lammens. He said: 'I knew it was a counter-attacking opportunity to drive, and I think Estevao made the run on the outside. I was just going to keep driving and I was looking to play him, but then the space just kind of opened up and I just kept going. 'Then it was just about being composed in front of goal and luckily it went in.' The goal came at an important moment for the Blues, who had endured a difficult first half before taking control after the interval. Cole Palmer subsequently doubled our advantage from the penalty spot, securing a welcome victory following recent setbacks against Tottenham Hotspur and Liverpool. While Rogers was pleased with the quality of his finish, he took even greater satisfaction from helping his side secure all three points. 'It was nice to see it go in the back of the net at an important time in the game,' he added. 'So that's the most important thing for me, that I can make a difference to the game and ultimately we go on and win the game because of it, so I'm happy.' Having embraced a new challenge following two years at Aston Villa, Rogers is enjoying life at Chelsea and believes the squad will continue developing together. 'I'm loving it. It's a different challenge, a new challenge, and I'm really enjoying playing with these wonderful quality players. 'It's just about the team coming together as a whole. There are some good times, bad times, but I've just got to be a bit of a leader, stick to what I know and do the best I can. So we just need to keep going.'

news.title: 'We need to keep winning'
Bjorn reflects on a special afternoon
Walsh excited by Chelsea's free-flowing attack after Charlton victory
news.body_en: Keira Walsh believes Chelsea's attacking play is becoming increasingly free-flowing after producing a moment of individual brilliance in our emphatic 6-0 Women's Super League victory over Charlton Athletic. The England international was at the heart of another impressive performance from Sonia Bompastor's side, producing an audacious backheel assist for Aggie Beever-Jones as the Blues returned to the top of the WSL table. Chelsea scored four times inside the opening 19 minutes at The Valley before adding two more after the interval, and Walsh believes the confidence running through the squad is helping our attacking players flourish. 'I think the whole team feels confident,' said Walsh. 'I think some of the goals we scored today were really, really good. 'I think the team's just in a really, really good place. And I think especially in attack, it feels very free-flowing. I'm excited about it.' Walsh's creativity was on full display in the 57th minute when she improvised brilliantly to flick the ball into Beever-Jones' path, allowing the striker to finish clinically and register her first goal of the campaign. While the midfielder admitted her inventive pass was not necessarily intended for Beever-Jones, she was delighted to help her team-mate get among the goals. 'I was just trying to flick it for one of the runners in behind. I probably saw Sandy more, to be honest! I think it was a really good finish from Aggie. 'I think giving our strikers confidence, giving our forwards confidence to know that they can score those goals again, is really important.' Another player who enjoyed a memorable afternoon was Giulia Dragoni, who came off the bench to score her first competitive Chelsea goal with a superb finish in the 66th minute. Walsh, who previously crossed paths with the young Italian during her time at Barcelona, was full of praise for her team-mate's ability and attitude. 'For me, she's just an incredible person. I think she's just the best team-mate to have in the changing room. 'I think probably for her, she's been a little bit disappointed in her minutes, if she's being honest. But I think in terms of what she does for the team and the players who are playing, she's incredible. 'I think since she's come to Chelsea, she's been such a good talent in training. And I think you can see with her first touch and her finish. Her body was almost facing the opposite way and she could still find the bottom corner.' The midfielder also highlighted the collective joy at seeing Dragoni score, with the celebrations reflecting the close-knit nature of Bompastor's squad. 'I think you could see how happy the bench was for Giulia when she scored. So I think it just shows the togetherness of the team in general.' Despite our six-goal haul, Walsh was equally pleased with the defensive discipline shown by the Blues ahead of another important run of fixtures. 'I think a clean sheet was important today. I think that's something we've really been focusing on this year. And obviously scoring a lot of goals. 'Important going into some big games coming up. Really happy with the team performance.'

news.title: WSL Full Match: Charlton Athletic Women vs Chelsea Women
Estevao's Brazilian magic
Bompastor provides Lauren James injury update and praises Blues after Charlton win
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed Lauren James will undergo further assessment after the Chelsea forward suffered a hamstring problem during our emphatic 6-0 Women's Super League victory over Charlton Athletic. James had been influential as the Blues raced into a four-goal lead inside the opening 19 minutes at The Valley, but pulled up while running for a through ball and was replaced by Erin Cuthbert shortly after the half-hour mark. Speaking after the game, Bompastor admitted it was too early to determine the severity of the injury. She said: 'It is difficult to say. I can only say it's her hamstring and we'll assess her later to have more detailed information. We'll probably need to assess her tomorrow. 'I think it's her hamstring, so we'll see what happens from tomorrow.' Despite that setback, there were plenty of positives for our head coach, including a memorable afternoon for Nathalie Bjorn. The Swedish defender captained the Blues on her first WSL start since November 2025 and marked her return with a towering header to open the scoring inside three minutes. 'Today I'm really pleased for Nat Bjorn,' said Bompastor. 'She's been injured for so long and she hasn't played much football in the past year. So I think for her to start the game and score an early goal was a big boost for her confidence, so it's nice.' Another player who enjoyed a special moment was Giulia Dragoni, who came off the bench to score her first competitive Chelsea goal with a superb finish in the 66th minute. The young Italian was visibly emotional after finding the net, and Bompastor believes her dedication behind the scenes made the moment particularly rewarding. Bompastor said: 'I think the emotion after the goal comes from the fact that she's been working really, really hard. 'She's a young talent. She had the opportunity to show that today when she came on, but also with the goal she scored. 'It's a great goal. The competition is high right now in the squad and she needs to stay patient. Even if today was a good 30 minutes on the pitch for her, a really positive performance, that's the only thing she can control. 'She can keep doing that to give me some headaches!'

news.title: Penders: It’s about how you react to setbacks
news.body_en: Mike Penders believes learning from mistakes is an important part of his development after bouncing back from a difficult afternoon against Tottenham Hotspur to help Chelsea secure a 2-0 victory over Manchester United. The Belgian goalkeeper endured disappointment in last weekend’s defeat to Spurs, when an unfortunate own-goal from a corner helped the visitors claim all three points at Stamford Bridge. But the 21-year-old has responded impressively, producing a string of fine saves against Liverpool in midweek before keeping a clean sheet in Saturday’s Premier League triumph over United. ‘To have something like that is part of football and part of my journey,’ Penders reflected on the Tottenham setback. ‘You will make mistakes, but then it’s about how you react, and I am very happy I could bring some positivity on the pitch today.’ Penders certainly played his part in our return to winning ways, making important interventions as United threatened during a closely contested first half. He twice denied Amad Diallo before producing arguably his finest moment deep into stoppage time, getting his fingertips to Bryan Mbeumo’s powerful effort from distance and diverting the ball onto the crossbar. It was a superb piece of goalkeeping that preserved our two-goal advantage and ensured the Blues finished the afternoon with a clean sheet. ‘It was a very hard shot and I didn’t see him coming,’ Penders explained. ‘But in the end, I was able to get my fingers onto it and I was very happy [to make that save].’ The victory was particularly welcome after consecutive defeats against Tottenham and Liverpool, the latter coming via a penalty shoot-out in the Carabao Cup. Penders was pleased with the character shown by Xabi Alonso’s side in responding to those setbacks. ‘I think as a team as well, we have reacted very well after the last two games. I think against Liverpool we played a good game, and today we did a great job.’ Saturday’s contest was far from straightforward, with United having a first-half goal from Matheus Cunha ruled out for offside. However, Morgan Rogers broke the deadlock shortly after the interval with a superb individual effort before Cole Palmer doubled our advantage from the penalty spot. For Penders, the key to securing all three points was maintaining composure, even when the visitors threatened. ‘I think we just played our football. We stayed calm and were very controlled in our game. I think that was very important. ‘Of course, sometimes they have chances. For example, the goal that was disallowed in the first half. But it’s important to keep your head in the game and that’s what we did. It was a good win for us.’

news.title: Match report: Charlton Athletic 0-6 Chelsea Women
news.body_en: Chelsea returned to the top of the Women's Super League with a commanding 6-0 victory over Charlton Athletic, scoring four times inside the opening 19 minutes at The Valley. Captain Nathalie Bjorn headed us in front on her first league start for almost a year, before Melvine Malard struck twice either side of an Ellie Carpenter goal as the Blues raced into a four-goal lead. Half-time substitute Aggie Beever-Jones added a fifth, and Giulia Dragoni rounded off the scoring with her first competitive Chelsea goal to complete a dominant afternoon for Sonia Bompastor's side. The emphatic victory also extended our unbeaten start to the WSL campaign and moved us back above Manchester City on goal difference, after our title rivals had won earlier in the day. The only concern came when Lauren James, who had been outstanding during our blistering start, was forced off with an injury before half-time. Bompastor made seven changes from Wednesday's 2-0 UEFA Women's Champions League victory over Roma, with Bjorn returning to captain the side in her first WSL start since November 2025. The Sweden international has endured a frustrating spell with injuries but marked another significant step in her return to regular action in spectacular fashion. There was also a first Chelsea start for Manaka Matsukubo. The Japan international joined from North Carolina Courage during the summer, having been named the NWSL Midfielder of the Year in 2025, and made her Blues debut as a late substitute against Crystal Palace last weekend. Carpenter, Katie McCabe, Keira Walsh, Sjoeke Nusken and Malard were among the other players brought into the starting XI. We took just three minutes to break the deadlock. McCabe received the ball following a short corner and floated an inviting delivery into the penalty area, where Bjorn climbed highest to send a firm header into the net. We continued to pour forward and doubled our advantage in the 10th minute. Sandy Baltimore, a constant source of danger on the left, delivered a cross which struck Malard around the midriff and slipped past Charlton goalkeeper Anna Koivunen. Three minutes later, James tested Koivunen with an effort from outside the area. The goalkeeper could only push the ball into Carpenter's path, and the Australian finished confidently from close range for her fifth goal in all competitions this season. Matsukubo then passed up a promising opening as she searched for her first Chelsea goal, but there was little respite for the hosts. The fourth arrived in the 19th minute following a scramble in the Charlton box. Koivunen made a couple of saves as the Blues sought another way through, only for Malard to react quickest to the loose ball and turn home from a matter of yards. The French forward thought she had completed her hat-trick shortly afterwards, racing onto a superb James pass and finishing across goal, but the assistant referee's flag ruled it out for offside. James had been instrumental in our attacking display but was forced to pull up while running off the ball just after the half-hour mark and could not continue. Erin Cuthbert came on in her place. There was also a brief interruption when Nusken needed treatment after catching her finger on an advertising board. Charlton gradually steadied themselves after the opening onslaught and Jodie Hutton headed an opportunity off target, although Chelsea still enjoyed around 70 per cent of possession in the first half and did not allow the hosts a shot on target. Bompastor introduced Beever-Jones for Malard at half-time and Beever-Jones took her opportunity just before the hour mark. Walsh produced an inventive, instinctive backheel to send the forward through, and she finished calmly to register her first goal of the season, celebrating with visible delight. Bjorn, Walsh and Matsukubo were then withdrawn as Bompastor made three further changes, but the Blues remained on the front foot. Baltimore curled a wonderful effort against the woodwork, leaving Koivunen stranded, before Maika Hamano was denied by the post just moments later. Our sixth finally arrived in the 66th minute, when Dragoni finished a flowing move involving fellow substitutes with real composure. The young Italian, who joined Chelsea permanently from Barcelona in the summer, was overcome with emotion as she celebrated her first competitive goal for the club. Koivunen, making her WSL debut, recovered from a difficult opening to produce some impressive saves, including an excellent stop to deny Alyssa Thompson in the closing stages. Charlton continued to search for a consolation and Ashleigh Neville headed narrowly over from a late corner, but Hannah Hampton and the Blues defence held firm to secure a clean sheet. Chelsea have now won seven of our opening eight WSL matches, drawing the other, and return to the summit with 22 points. Our goal difference of plus 23 puts us ahead of Manchester City, who also have 22 points. We welcome Everton to Stamford Bridge in the Women's Super League on Saturday 7 November, with kick-off scheduled for 12.45pm. Chelsea: Hampton, Carpenter, Bjorn (c) (Thompson 62), Buurman, McCabe, Walsh (Dragoni 61), Nusken, Matsukubo (Hamano 62), James (Cuthbert 35), Baltimore, Malard (Beever-Jones HT)Unused substitutes: Peng, Buchanan, Bronze, KapteinGoalscorers: Bjorn 3, Malard 10, 19, Carpenter 13, Beever-Jones 57, Dragoni 66 Charlton Athletic: Koivunen, Johnston (Robe 79), Skeels (c), Lobato, Mason (Waldie 58), Neville, van Egmond (Kenney 46), Flannery, Hutton (Lockwood 73), Korhonen (Fitzgerald 58), DavidsonUnused substitutes: Whitehouse, Nelson-Iye, Humphrey, AzzaroBooked: Hutton 50

news.title: Cole Palmer: People don't realise how good Romeo Lavia is
news.body_en: Cole Palmer has described Romeo Lavia as one of his favourite midfielders in the world and believes his team-mate continues to be underappreciated by some. The Belgian midfielder was instrumental in Saturday's win, offering composure and quality in the centre of the pitch as the Blues improved after the interval to secure all three points. Lavia also helped create our opening goal, winning the ball back and feeding Morgan Rogers, who surged forward and lifted a fine finish over United goalkeeper Senne Lammens. And Palmer, who later doubled our advantage from the penalty spot, reserved special praise for his team-mate after the final whistle. 'Today was one of the best games I've seen him play,' said Palmer. 'I've said all along he's one of my favourite midfielders, and people still don't realise how good he is. 'Obviously he's had his injury problems, but he's trying to put that behind him now and put in performances like today. I thought he was the best player on the pitch.' Lavia's display was particularly encouraging given the injury setbacks which have interrupted his Chelsea career, with the 22-year-old now looking to build momentum through consistent performances. While it was a memorable afternoon for Lavia, the Blues had to work hard for the result. United created openings before the break, but our second-half response proved decisive. After Rogers opened the scoring, Palmer made it 2-0 from the spot following Lisandro Martinez's dismissal, and the Blues saw out the match to earn an important clean sheet. Reflecting on the team's performance, Palmer said: 'It was a tough first half, but I think second half we stepped up and I'm happy with the three points. 'Certainly [in the second half] we were less sloppy with the chances they were getting from us losing the ball. So we just played harder and created our chances.'

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Charlton Athletic
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made seven changes to her Chelsea side for this afternoon's Barclays Women's Super League clash with Charlton Athletic at The Valley. Following our 2-0 UEFA Women's Champions League victory over Roma in midweek, the Blues return to domestic action with a trip across London to face the newly-promoted Addicks. Hannah Hampton retains her place in goal, with Nathalie Bjorn and Katie McCabe returning to the starting XI alongside Veerle Buurman. Ellie Carpenter also comes into the side after scoring in Wednesday's European victory. There are changes in midfield, with Sjoeke Nusken, Keira Walsh and Manaka Matsukubo all named in the starting line-up, while Erin Cuthbert and Wieke Kaptein are among the substitutes. Lauren James and Sandy Baltimore retain their places, with Melvine Malard returning to the starting XI after scoring twice in our last league outing against Crystal Palace. The Blues will be looking to maintain our unbeaten start to the Women's Super League season when we kick off at The Valley at 2.30pm. You can follow all the action as it happens in our Match Centre, while those in the UK can watch the game on BBC Two, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website. Chelsea: Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter, Nathalie Bjorn (c), Veerle Buurman, Katie McCabe, Sjoeke Nusken, Keira Walsh, Manaka Matsukubo, Lauren James, Sandy Baltimore, Melvine Malard. Chelsea substitutes: Livia Peng, Lucy Bronze, Kadeisha Buchanan, Erin Cuthbert, Giulia Dragoni, Wieke Kaptein, Maika Hamano, Alyssa Thompson, Aggie Beever-Jones.

news.title: CFC Unlocked | Morgan Rogers 🔓
The Haunted Cottage
What a performance from Romeo!
Xabi Alonso reflects on a 'very important' clean sheet and stable Mike Penders
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has emphasised the importance of the Blues keeping our second clean sheet in three Premier League matches and highlighted Mike Penders’ role in our victory over Manchester United. Our shutout in yesterday's game at Stamford Bridge was hard-earned. The visitors, particularly in the opening 45 minutes, created several goalscoring opportunities and Penders was tested on several occasions. He produced good stops to deny Amad Diallo, but the best came late in the game. With the Blues leading by two goals after Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer had found the net, Bryan Mbeumo rasped a 20-yard drive toward our goal. Penders produced a full-length dive as the ball ricocheted off the crossbar and was cleared. Only the slow-motion replay showed that the Belgian goalkeeper had got a small but decisive touch on the ball to divert it onto the woodwork and preserve our clean sheet. Alonso insisted that should not be taken lightly, with the Blues manager explaining after our win: '[The clean sheet] is very important, and it’s the second one in three Premier League games. 'We need many more and we don’t take them for granted. Three points and a clean sheet is good and we need to keep on repeating this scoreline.’ On Penders, he added: ‘Not just today, I think at Liverpool he was really solid. Mike had a very good performance today and was very stable for a goalkeeper. 'He has shown a good level [against Man United], and we kept another clean sheet, the second one in three games. Now we need to keep going. 'Mike has overcome the difficult moment that we had last Saturday and this is part of the development of any goalkeeper, or any player.’ The Blues return home after the international break to take on our old rivals, Leeds United. news.title: Romeo Lavia on hard work paying off with ‘statement performance’
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia believes Chelsea’s performance in the 2-0 victory over Manchester United laid down a marker for what he and the Blues are capable of this season. The Belgian was in fine form as we got back to winning ways at Stamford Bridge on Saturday and played an important part in the opening goal shortly after half-time. It was Lavia who halted a United attack with a crucial tackle and then reacted quickly to nip in and send the loose ball to Morgan Rogers. From there, Rogers powered forward through the Man Utd defence and lifted a composed finish over the keeper. Cole Palmer then added a second from the penalty spot to extend our lead and ensure it was the Blues who would take all three points. For Lavia, it was a performance which further underlined his growing momentum in the Chelsea midfield, as he continues to put a difficult period with injury behind him. ‘I like to say that my job is to make the job for the other players in front of me easier, and everyone around me,’ reflected Lavia. ‘So I'm happy I've been able to do that and help the team to get a good win. ‘I feel very comfortable. Like I've always said, it's been in the weeks a lot of work that goes unseen with everyone in the building, at the training ground. So I'm very happy that it's all paying off and hopefully it just continues this way.’ The win at the Bridge saw Chelsea bounce back from the double disappointment of last week’s loss to Tottenham Hotspur and the midweek Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool on penalties, with the added bonus of returning the Blues to the top four of the Premier League table, at least until Liverpool’s meeting with Arsenal on Sunday. ‘It was a very important game and important win,’ Lavia continued. ‘I think the team effort was amazing. Everyone, from the players who started to the players who came on, was engaged and I think that’s a good statement for what's ahead. ‘It was quite obvious that the chances that they had in the first half were coming from our mistakes, sometimes rushing things a little bit when we had the control. So the message was just to rectify that little detail in the second half and for the rest not to change anything. I think we did that and we got the clean sheet as well, so it's a very good win. ‘We’re very happy with the win, but we're not overthinking things. We are very focused and we know that it's a process. It's a good day, but a performance like this is a good statement of what we're capable of delivering.’ With Lavia completing his second full 90 minutes in the space of four days and Chelsea making it three wins from our last four Premier League games, it seems he and the team are beginning to hit their stride just as we approach the busy winter period. news.title: PL Extended: Chelsea 2-0 Man Utd
Full Match: Chelsea vs Manchester United
Alonso reveals Estevao plan after Brazilian's 'best response' against Man United
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso revealed Estevao Willian was told he would start against Manchester United at the beginning of the week, and praised the Brazilian for showing the ‘best response’ in our 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge. The 19-year-old was handed his first Premier League start of the campaign in today's lunchtime kick-off and produced an impressive display. He twice had the ball in the back of the net – only to be denied by the assistant referee and VAR – registered six shots, the joint-most by a Chelsea player in a top-flight game this season, and created three chances. Those inside Stamford Bridge gave Estevao a standing ovation when he was replaced by Malo Gusto in the closing minutes. Before he took his seat in the dugout, Estevao and Alonso shared a warm embrace. He was then congratulated by the Blues coaching staff and his team-mates. And after the victory, Alonso explained he had outlined to Estevao after last weekend's game against Tottenham Hotspur, and before our midweek Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool, that he had earmarked the Brazil international to start against United. ‘We knew earlier this week – you ask me but sometimes I can’t give you all the info,' Alonso said with a smile. 'We spoke after Tottenham and he knew he was going to be playing today. 'He had the best response and showed that he deserves more and that he was prepared, and that is what we want from our players. So we're very happy for him. He deserves to enjoy this game; he had a good connection with the crowd and was really close to scoring his goal. He fought really hard and at the end he was tired, but it has been a good day for him.’ With Joao Pedro sidelined due to a thigh injury, Alonso has had to tweak his frontline in our last three outings. He opted for Pedro Neto to lead his attack against United, with Estevao, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers in support. It was Rogers who broke the deadlock with a fine solo run. Palmer later converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez had been sent off for a foul on Wesley Fofana. ‘I assess different situations, from what we were going to do against Liverpool, and what we were going to do [against Manchester United],' explained Alonso. 'I had an idea [that Estevao would start], and I had it clear that he could have a good impact today, and he has shown it. 'He was a threat, he created many chances and situations where we could score. He has shown it well today.' The Blues return home after the international break to take on our old rivals, Leeds United. Secure your place early with Club Chelsea. VIP tickets available now.

news.title: Cole Palmer on Rogers' impact against Man United and love for Estevao
news.body_en: Cole Palmer was full of praise for his Blues team-mate and friend Morgan Rogers after the duo scored the goals that gave Chelsea victory over Manchester United, and also had words for Estevao Willian after the Brazilian’s return to the starting XI. The Blues secured a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in Saturday’s early Premier League kick-off, with Palmer and Rogers helping make up for the absence of striker Joao Pedro by both finding the back of the net. Palmer did so from the penalty spot, getting his 50th Premier League goal for the club on his 105th appearance. Only Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Diego Costa have reached that landmark faster. That came after Rogers had opened the scoring early in the second half. Romeo Lavia won possession in midfield, allowing the England international to pick up the ball and carry it almost the entire length of the Man Utd half, before lifting a deft finish over goalkeeper Senne Lammens. ‘That's what he does, you know,’ Palmer responded with a shrug and a smirk when asked about Rogers’ latest stunning goal for the Blues. ‘He gets the ball between the lines and when he drives he makes things happen. He went all the way himself and it was a great finish.’ With Pedro Neto taking on the centre forward role against the Red Devils, Estevao Willian came into the attack on the wing, making his first Premier League start of the season. The Brazilian made the most of his opportunity, producing several eye-catching moments and finding the back of the net twice, only to have the goals ruled out for offside, the second for the narrowest of VAR calls. ‘He needed to be patient for his moment and he got his moment today,’ Cole said of Estevao’s performance. ‘You could see in moments he was very good. ‘He was unlucky with the offside; I think it was literally a centimetre. But we know the talent he's got and we all love him. So hopefully he can continue like that.’ It was an important three points for Chelsea, dismissing the memories of last week’s loss to Tottenham Hotspur and the midweek Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool on penalties. The result also moves us back into the top four – at least temporarily – and makes it three wins from four matches in the Premier League since the last international break. ‘It was very important to get back to winning ways, obviously after the last defeat, so it's good,’ added Palmer, before explaining what changed in the second half to allow us to break the deadlock and win the game. ‘I just think we were more intense. The chances they had were from us losing the ball, so we tried to play a bit smarter, a bit sharper and not losing the ball as easily, and I think it helped.’ The Blues return home after the international break to take on our old rivals, Leeds United. news.title: Match gallery: United fall at the Bridge
PL Highlights: Chelsea 2-0 Man Utd
'We reacted at half-time'
'The team spirit was immense'
Xabi Alonso reveals half-time instruction that helped Blues defeat Man United
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso praised the reaction of his Chelsea players against Manchester United after stressing his side needed to ‘win this game with the ball’ at half-time in our 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge. For 45 minutes at Stamford Bridge, little separated the two sides. Possession was evenly shared and while we registered seven shots, three of which were on target, United managed nine, with Mike Penders worked on three occasions. However, after the break, it was a different story. We broke the deadlock in the 50th minute through a fine solo goal from Morgan Rogers and doubled our advantage when Cole Palmer converted from the penalty spot after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a foul on Wesley Fofana. Naturally, United's reduction to 10 men influenced how the contest played out, but we had 67 per cent of the ball in the second period and fired 11 shots at the United goal. The visitors, in contrast, managed just three. Alonso emphasised after the win that, at the interval, he had stressed to his players the importance of controlling the game through possession, which he felt his players implemented impressively. ‘I think that there were different moments in the game,' the Blues manager said. 'The first half was intense, with momentum for both sides. United had their chances and we were close as well. At half-time, we spoke and the reaction in the second half was better. 'We started quite well, got the lead, and we looked in better control. After it went 2-0 and the red card the context of the game changed, but it was not easy.’ Alonso continued: 'When we spoke at half-time, we said we were going to win this game with the ball, so the improvement has been with the ball. The message was to be better with the ball and to not give away that much. 'We changed some tactical things, but we were more comfortable on the pitch with better control. When you feel better with the ball, normally the better you are defending as well. 'So I think that reaction, that change, has been important for the feeling and the goal as well.’ Alonso opted to start without an orthodox striker against United. Pedro Neto was tasked with leading the line, while Palmer, Rogers and Estevao Willian operated effectively behind the Portuguese international. 'We need to be creative sometimes to find solutions with the players available,' said the Blues manager. 'Pedro has worked really hard in that position. It’s not new to him, linking up with the players around him. 'There were moments [in the first half], but I would say, especially at the start of the second half and what we had spoken about at half-time, the reaction was good.' The Blues return home after the international break to take on our old rivals, Leeds United. Secure your place early with Club Chelsea. VIP tickets available now.

news.title: Match report: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United
news.body_en: A wonderful individual goal from Morgan Rogers and a Cole Palmer penalty were enough for the Blues to see off 10-man Manchester United at Stamford Bridge and get back to winning ways in the Premier League. The 90 minutes certainly didn't lack drama. Nor goalscoring opportunities. In the opening period, Estevao Willian had the ball in the net for the Blues, as did Matheus Cunha for United. Yet the goals were both ruled out for offside. Xabi Alonso's side took control after the break – and we broke the deadlock in some style. Rogers collected the ball in midfield, breezed past Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez, and clipped a finish over Senne Lammens. Our second arrived in the 64th minute, with Palmer converting from 12 yards. The penalty was awarded after a VAR review for Martinez elbowing Wesley Fofana from a corner. The Argentine defender was shown a second yellow card and a red for the incident. With a man and a two-goal advantage, the Blues were certain of the points. We appeared to have added a third goal when Estevao powered a finish into the roof of the net, but he was denied by a VAR review for offside. It didn't change the outcome of the contest, as after two painful defeats in league and cup, we got back on track and claimed the three points. Alonso made four alterations to his side. Marco Palestra made his first Premier League start, Levi Colwill returned to the defence, and Palmer and Estevao Willian were included in the attack. Malo Gusto, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson, who was absent through illness, and Danny Welbeck dropped out of the starting XI The opening 45 minutes ebbed and flowed. The Blues fashioned chances; United did the same. Sustained pressure was fleeting. Estevao fired the first warning shot of the afternoon. The winger cut inside onto his stronger right foot and whipped a shot toward the far corner. Senne Lammens was beaten, but the ball flew wide. United responded with an attempt of their own. A neat move around our penalty box saw Bruno Fernandes tee up former Blue Andrey Santos, and the midfielder guided a shot narrowly wide. Throughout the opening period, opportunities arrived via counter-attacks, and in the 14th minute, one led to what appeared to be our opening goal. Estevao launched a break and fed Pedro Neto, who forced a save from Lammens. The Brazilian converted the rebound from close range, only for the offside flag to be raised. From United's next attack, launched following a Chelsea corner, Bryan Mbeumo played an expertly weighted crossfield pass to Fernandes. The Portuguese controlled but skewed his shot high and wide. Fernandes looked to return the favour to Mbeumo soon after, flashing the ball across the Blues' six-yard box. Yet the United forward couldn't react to finish. It was a let-off. A flurry of United chances followed. First, Mike Penders reacted well to push clear a powerful low shot from Amad Diallo, and Josh Acheampong did well on the rebound to deny Matheus Cunha. Amad then forced Penders into a near-post stop. A key moment in the game arrived ten minutes before the interval. Maguire met a back-post corner and Matheus Cunha was able to nod the ball past Penders from close range. The United forward celebrated, as did his team-mates. Then came a VAR review: the Brazilian was offside and the goal was ruled out. United continued to threaten, and Amad twice came close either side of Moises Caicedo striking the base of the post from an Estevao corner. Wesley Fofana denied the United winger with an excellent block, and from his second attempt, the winger missed a one-on-one with Penders. The final opportunities of the opening period were ours. Neto first robbed Maguire in his own defensive third, broke into the box and tried to finish. Unfortunately, his far-post attempt flew wide. Estevao then drew a save from Lammens to draw the half to a close. Alonso opted against any substitutions at the break – and five minutes after the restart was rewarded as the Blues broke the deadlock. It was quite the goal. The impressive Romeo Lavia did excellently to win back possession in midfield and laid a pass to Rogers, who began to advance 35 yards from goal. The England international wasn't challenged, then eased beyond Maguire and Martinez into the box, and lifted a deft finish over Lammens. With momentum and confidence, the Blues then took – and did not relinquish – control. It was one-way traffic, with Penders hardly tested. Lammens was far busier. He first had to deny a header from Neto, and then had to be alert to avoid being caught out by an Estevao corner destined for the net. Pressure was building on the United goal. We earned a corner that Estevao delivered to the back post and, under pressure from Martinez, Fofana fell to the ground holding his face. Another corner was awarded, but VAR intervened. Referee Peter Bankes went to the monitor and, following a review, awarded a penalty. Martinez was shown a second yellow card and then a red. United were down to ten – and moments later were two goals behind as Palmer powered his spot-kick through Lammens. From then on, it was clear the three points would be staying at Stamford Bridge. Only the final scoreline was uncertain. The Blues supporters did have the chance to celebrate a third goal as, after winning the ball back in United's half, Palmer slipped a pass through to Estevao, who advanced and drilled a shot into the roof of the net. The Brazilian celebrated with his team-mates and Alonso, but following a delayed VAR review, the goal was ruled out for a marginal offside. Estevao was determined to get his name on the score-sheet, though, and twice forced Lammens into good stops. The second was a powerful effort that required a full-length stop. Alonso shuffled his pack as the half progressed. Pep Chavarria was introduced for Palestra; Malo Gusto, Valentin Barco and Danny Welbeck came on late for Caicedo, Estevao and Neto. Ten minutes were added. They didn't pass without incident. First, Mbeumo thumped a shot against the crossbar from 20 yards before the Blues cleared. Replays showed Penders got the merest of touches to deflect it onto the woodwork. An impressive run forward from Acheampong and a neat pass from Chavarria then presented Palmer with a chance, but he curled his effort over. Barco then missed the final chance of the contest, firing wide from close range after a Gusto cross. The Blues have a full week to prepare for our next top-flight fixture, which comes next weekend as we travel to Sunderland on 8 November. Our next home fixture is against Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday 21 November and you can secure your place at Stamford Bridge early with Club Chelsea, as VIP tickets are available here now. news.title: Under-18 Premier League report: West Ham 5-3 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s suffered our first defeat in almost two months as, despite goals from Heze Grimwade, Ibrahim Rabbaj and Riley Ebho, the Blues were beaten by West Ham United. We started superbly, asking plenty of questions of the hosts' backline, and broke the deadlock in the 26th minute through yet another Grimwade set piece. Rabbaj claimed our second with a placed finish into the left corner just after the half-hour mark, but the score was 2-1 at the break as Tyrone Omotoye pulled a goal back for the hosts. In the second period, we re-established our two-goal lead thanks to Ebho. Unfortunately, West Ham scored three goals in six minutes to make it 4-3 and, while we tried to equalise, the Hammers had the final say as they netted their fifth of the afternoon. The Blues came racing out the blocks, piling pressure on West Ham’s backline. Within seven minutes, we had earned three corners, and our pressure midway through the half was after Rabbaj received the ball on the right flank and made a darting run towards the penalty area. His quick feet and pace were too much for the West Ham defence, who were forced to foul the Moroccan in a dangerous area. Grimwade stepped up and continued to prove himself as a free-kick specialist, firing the ball into the far corner. Rabbaj extended our lead five minutes later, netting his first goal of the season. Jayden Malundama came close to marking his return to the starting eleven with a goal but was thwarted by Felix Lewis-Ayesta. The loose ball fell to the edge of the box and Rabbaj picked his spot perfectly. He almost had a brace before the interval when he spotted the Hammers keeper off his line at the start of another attack. Rabbaj went for the spectacular from the halfway line and wasn’t far away, his effort whistled just wide of the right post. However, in the final action of the half, West Ham made it 2-1 through Omotoye. Hungry for more in the second period, Rabbaj kept testing Lewis-Ayesta and troubling the opposition. We had an array of chances, with Andrew Pennie unlucky not to turn his header toward goal and Jashayde Greenwood a whisker away from close range. It was Ebho who got our third, though, as he collected the ball off Grimwade and let fly from distance. His effort took a deflection and beat Lewis-Ayesta to reinstate our two-goal advantage. It wasn't one we were able to keep, though. With 20 minutes remaining, we were caught in possession and Jude Longman halved the deficit once more. The Blues responded well initially, as Greenwood's thumping strike was tipped onto the crossbar by Lewis-Ayesta, earning us a corner. Unfortunately, we were caught on the counter and punished as Omotoye got his second of the afternoon and equalise for the Hammers. Moments after the leveller, we conceded a penalty which Longman converted to put us behind for the first time in the contest. We pushed for an equaliser but West Ham managed a fifth before the final whistle to inflict our first defeat since the start of September. This defeat sees us drop to 2nd position and remain on 21 points. We now trail the league leaders by two points. Chelsea Under-18s host Charlton Athletic in the Premier League Cup on Saturday 7 November at Cobham Training Ground. The game gets underway at 11am GMT and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Xabi Alonso explains Jordan Henderson absence against Man United
news.body_en: Ahead of facing Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, Xabi Alonso explained why Jordan Henderson isn’t involved and why now was the right time for Estevao Willian to come into the starting XI. Our manager made four changes to his line-up for today’s Premier League fixture, one of them enforced by the absence of Henderson from the matchday squad to face the Red Devils. ‘He's ill,’ revealed Alonso. ‘There’s no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday and today had a fever in the morning, so he was not feeling good enough to come with the team.’ In another of the changes, Alonso has called on Estevao, the Brazilian making his first league start of the 2026/27 season. When asked why now was the right time, our manager’s response was simple: ‘Because he's ready. ‘Because he's been preparing and training well to be ready any time, whenever he's needed, and today he's needed and we hope that he enjoys his game, and he can have a good impact.’ Estevao looks set to line up in a four-pronged Chelsea attack, alongside Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. However, when it comes to which of those forwards will lead the line as the central striker, Alonso is keeping his cards close to his chest. ‘It's too early to tell,’ the Spaniard said with a grin. ‘It’s too early, so we will see. It could be Morgan, but we have options.’

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea line up vs Manchester United
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has opted to make four changes to his Chelsea starting XI for this afternoon's Premier League meeting with Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. We return to top-flight action after midweek Carabao Cup heartache and host a Man United side that have won just one of their eight league fixtures this term. Mike Penders continues in goal for the Blues after an impressive showing at Liverpool on Wednesday night, and is set to be protected by a back four of Josh Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Marco Palestra, who makes his first Premier League start. Moises Caicedo captains the Blues and continues in midfield alongside Romeo Lavia. Jordan Henderson is not in the matchday squad. Estevao Willian comes into the Chelsea attack, Cole Palmer returns after serving a one-match suspension, and Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto start once again. news.title: U18 PL Full Match: West Ham U18s vs Chelsea U18s
Wieke Kaptein on her improvement this season and key to Blues' strong start
news.body_en: Wieke Kaptein has been a key cog in Sonia Bompastor’s side this season, often doing the unseen work that has given the Blues a platform on which to record victories. On Wednesday evening, Kaptein provided assists for both of our goals in our UEFA Women’s Champions League victory against Roma, and then claimed the Player of the Match trophy. It was the second individual accolade claimed by the Dutch international after our league phase matches; the first came after she scored a brilliant strike in our 1-0 victory over Austria Vienna. And although she was pleased with her performance at Plough Lane, she typically shifted the praise onto her team-mates. ‘It's a nice stadium. I like playing there,’ she told us. ‘Of course, I had two assists against Roma. But I think one of the defenders should have it, to be honest. Kadeisha (Buchanan), Lucy (Bronze), and Veerle (Buurman) did very well to get the clean sheet, and I think that's just as important as assists or the goals. ‘It’s nice to get the assists, though. I have a really good connection with Ellie (Carpenter). When she came in, we found each other very easily. Of course, I can do a lot of things better. I could hold the ball sometimes a little bit better, but everyone can learn.’ Kaptein speaks of a reset in the summer where she evaluated her own performances from last season and worked hard to improve. Her motivation was not only to earn more minutes, but also to contribute to the collective effort and allow others to shine. ‘It is my game, to be honest,’ she continues. ‘My team-mates see what I do for them, and that’s the only thing that’s important to me. My main strength is to make other players play at their best. ‘I'm on a good run right now: I feel good. I think if you see my statistics, I recover a lot of balls. I also like making key passes. I really like it when my teammates are feeling good on the pitch. That’s when I feel good on the pitch. ‘In the second half of last season, I didn't play as much, so I did a lot of work in pre-season. I work really hard and look at myself. I like to do the unselfish things in a game for the team, and I think that helps other players show their strengths. ‘I try to do that and also play my own game, making assists, and I hope to score a little bit more too. I want to be as important as I can be and help the team as much as I can. We have incredible midfielders this season. I think it's good; it keeps everyone sharp!’ While Kaptein has started all but one of our games this term, she sees the value of those brought on as substitutes. In our last two matches against Crystal Palace and Roma, those introduced have scored key second-half goals to help us to victory. The 21-year-old also points to the 6-2 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge. The game was level at 1-1 until a triple substitution just before the hour mark, another example of when the changes have worked to good effect. ‘I think the key, to be honest, is that we’re performing really well as a team,’ she explains. ‘The starters and the substitutes are just as important. It doesn't really matter who plays, but usually our substitutions make a difference in the game, and I think that's what has changed games a lot this season. ‘You could see it against Tottenham; they played well against us for 60 minutes, and then we brought our substitutes on, and we scored five goals. We're helping each other. Everyone wants to fight for each other, and I think that's really changed this year.’ We travel to Charlton tomorrow to face a side yet to score a point in their seven matches since being promoted from the second tier last summer. But Kaptein knows only too well that the Blues must not be complacent, no matter who we come up against. ‘They are fighting for points,’ she says. ‘So we need to be ready for them. We need to be consistent and focus on our own performances. We don't need to score in the first or second minute. We need to get the goal and then keep going.'

news.title: U18 Highlights: West Ham U18 5-3 Chelsea U18
Jordan Henderson on 'big moments' and playing alongside Moises Caicedo
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson talks about finding his feet at Chelsea in an exclusive interview with the matchday programme for today’s game against Manchester United. The midfielder hit the ground running with a brace on his home debut earlier this month, and speaks about the sensation of seeing the ball hit the back of the net less than two minutes into the 5-1 win over Bournemouth. 'You can never prepare for stuff like that,' he says. 'It was quite emotional for me because I’ve been out for so long and then coming to start at Chelsea and having to wait a little bit. 'So it was a big moment for me personally, but it was just something that I’d dreamt of over the few months that I’ve been here… that I could get a good start, and thankfully it happened in the first couple of minutes.' He also talks in depth about his midfield role under Xabi Alonso and the joy of playing alongside Moises Caicedo. 'I think it’s been a little bit different to what I’ve done in the past, playing a little bit of a double pivot with Moi,' he says. 'But when you play with somebody like Moi, he makes it so easy. 'He’s a world-class midfielder, probably one of the best in the world in his position. So for me it’s trying to help him and have a good relationship with him as much as possible, and he’s an incredible player to play with, which makes it easier for me.' This is our last home game before Remembrance Sunday and the programme pays tribute to the Chelsea players who lost their lives in the two world wars, while there is a special Legacy feature on events at the club during the Second World War. We also have all the info you need ahead of a massive match with Manchester United, and as it’s our 200th game against the Red Devils, we’ve picked out five outstanding Chelsea victories from among them. Meanwhile, our Greatest Games feature focuses on the Blues’ unforgettable 5-0 win in this fixture in October 1999. With all the latest from around the club, plus columns from the manager and the captain, we’ve got your matchday covered. Pick up your copy from the programme sellers around Stamford Bridge, or order online from our official publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Chelsea vs Man Utd | Ready for a thriller 👻
Xabi Alonso explains why Jorrel Hato will miss Manchester United
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has explained why Jorrel Hato will miss tomorrow’s match against Manchester United and discussed how the Blues can get the best out of our attacking talent on the big stage. Hato has been named in Alonso’s starting XI for six of our eight Premier League fixtures this season, but was absent for our midweek Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. The Dutch defender will also not feature when Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge for tomorrow's early kick-off, with Alonso confirming the nature of the 20-year-old's issue. ‘How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow,’ our manager confirmed in his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon. ‘He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.’ One player who is available to face United is Cole Palmer, who returns after serving his one-match suspension on Wednesday. Palmer inspired a brilliant late comeback win over the Red Devils two years ago, when his hat-trick helped secure a dramatic 4-3 victory which will live long in the memory. Chelsea against Manchester United is always a big occasion, with two of English football’s most successful clubs go head-to-head, and Alonso went explained what the Blues need to do to help Palmer and his fellow attacking players shine once again in the intensity and pressure of a big-game atmosphere. ‘For sure, I think that everyone needs to show their best level in all the games, but in the big ones, sometimes it's harder because the opponent has good quality, because of the quality of the game,’ he added. ‘We need to support the attackers, so that they get the ball in the right place, so that they are involved, so that they are connected to the game and with the rest of the team. So we are all just focused on playing a good game tomorrow.’ Of course, Alonso is no stranger to big games in the Premier League, both as a player and a manager. During his time representing Liverpool, he was involved in many high-pressure encounters with Manchester United, in many of which he came up against fellow midfielder - and current United manager - Michael Carrick. ‘They were top games when I was at Liverpool, and they were intense games,’ the Spaniard recalled. ‘That United team was a top one and I remember playing against Michael. He was one of the finest English midfielders of that time. I really enjoyed playing against him before, at Spurs, and after at United with Paul Scholes. They had a fantastic midfield partnership. ‘So I really enjoyed playing against them and probably they made me a better player.’ Don't miss out! news.title: Xabi Alonso: ‘I want to see the good version of us’
news.body_en: At the end of a demanding week, Xabi Alonso has called on his Chelsea players to return to winning ways by ‘playing with personality’ against Manchester United and concentrating on what we can control. Last weekend, we suffered a rare home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur and then exited the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Wednesday, losing on penalties after a hard-fought 1-1 draw. The outcomes of the two games were disappointing, but Alonso saw improvements from his side in midweek. Now he wants to see us build on those foundations for Manchester United's visit in tomorrow's lunchtime kick-off. ‘It's a big one,’ the Blues manager said in his pre-match press conference. ‘We didn’t have much time to prepare, but it’s really important after the last home game that we keep winning games, and we have this winning feeling. ‘We need to have good control, good emotional control, be comfortable, be intense, control their quality. ‘They have many players that get close to each other when they have good connections. We need to be aware of that and we need to be brave and play our game with personality. The first goal...it's going to be important as well.’ Alonso would have ideally liked a longer turnaround between Wednesday night’s game on Merseyside and the return of Premier League action. However, he insisted his players will be ‘in the best possible condition for tomorrow’ physically and mentally. Alonso explained that part of his pre-match discussions with his squad have centred on ignoring the outside noise regarding tomorrow's visitors, who are fresh off 4-1 and 3-0 losses to Como and Bournemouth respectively. Our manager hopes last weekend’s result serves as a learning in that respect. He said: ‘It doesn't change the situation. We need to prepare the same way. We control what we can control. It's our preparation, our decisions, our mindset, knowing that they're a good team. ‘Against Tottenham, we said the table doesn't matter. At this moment, it doesn't matter. It's too early to tell. And United have a good squad; they have good players and a good manager. It’s going to be a tough game, and we’ll have a good version of us to win the game. ‘This is going to be the journey. We'll have good moments, tough moments, but we need to learn from them. I saw a better version of us on Wednesday than I saw on Saturday, even if the result wasn’t good in either, but I want to see more of the good version of us.’ Don't miss out! news.title: Training gallery: All together for United
Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Charlton press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash against Charlton on Sunday, and here are the key talking points from what the Blues head coach said. After confirming that Lexi Potter would not feature against Charlton, Bompastor explained that the 20-year-old would likely be back in action quickly after suffering a minor knee injury in the final stages of the win against Roma. The head coach has made full use of her substitutes to give the players the rest they need this season, and we remain unbeaten in all competitions after 12 games played. Here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Friday. 'It's important. When you have that ability, your team is a little bit more unpredictable. In the different teams I have coached, in my previous club as well, we always had a lot of players involved in scoring goals. 'The way we want to perform and play, it helps to get everyone involved and take some responsibility for scoring goals. I'm happy with that because sometimes it's difficult to rely on one person. If you do have a player who is on fire and scores every week and every game, it's also positive.' 'We come into every game really well prepared. We know in this league every game is tough, and you can lose points against anyone. We want to put in a good performance to get the three points. 'If we want to compete and stay at the top for as long as possible, we need to approach every game with a lot of respect for every opponent.' 'We reflected a lot after last season, and we knew exactly the things we wanted to improve. Having players performing at their best level helps a lot. 'If you look at the profiles we have in the squad, they are top-class players. That's in terms of their mentality, the desire to defend, the leadership they have, the communication they bring on the pitch, but also the quality they bring individually in winning the duels. 'It's about managing the backline and the whole team, managing the depth, the height of the block on the pitch; all these details are really well managed. We still have room for improvement, but I'm really pleased with the individual performances in the backline.' 'We are really happy to have Katie with us. Her leadership on and off the pitch is unbelievable. Working with Katie is really easy. 'She always wants to work hard. She always leads by example, and you can really have honest and direct conversations with her. 'Her performances on the pitch, how she is with the team and in the environment shows she always thinks first about the team and how she can help the team to be the best.' 'In the last two games, I was convinced I had to change the profiles of players coming into the game. That's why against Palace, I felt on the left side, having a player like Sandy (Baltimore) who is really comfortable in tight spaces and crossing from no space, I was convinced it was the right thing to do from what I could observe in the first half. 'In the game against Roma, I was also really convinced about bringing Ellie (Carpenter) in from half-time. It's always a tough balance because sometimes if you give some more minutes to the players on the pitch in the first half, maybe they will find their feet and deliver something more efficient. 'In the second half, sometimes spaces are more open because the other team is more fatigued. But when you have quality on the bench, you also need to trust the players who can come in and impact the game.'

news.title: Cobham Unseen: pre-Man Utd (h) 🎃
Bompastor Press Conference 🎙️
Bompastor updates on Lexi Potter ahead of Charlton
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor was pleased to confirm Lexi Potter’s knee injury is not serious, and while the midfielder will likely miss the game against Charlton, our head coach hopes to have her back before too long. The Blues face yet another London derby this weekend, this time against newly-promoted Charlton at The Valley. We sit at the top of the WSL table after seven games, equal on points with Manchester City on 19, but with a superior goal difference. We come into the game off the back of the midweek European victory against Roma. The only disappointment on the night was an injury picked up by Potter late on, but Bompastor reported it is not as bad as it could have been. ‘Lexi did an MRI yesterday evening and nothing major from her knee, so it’s good news,’ said the head coach at her media conference at Cobham. ‘She probably won’t be available for this weekend. We just need things to settle down a little bit, but nothing major. ‘We will see how she improves next week, and if she can be available for the Everton game.’ So far this season Bompastor has benefitted from having a largely fit squad to pick from, in contrast to the 2025/26 campaign. Managing players’ loads is of course a crucial component of her management, and she explained why the quality on display in the Women’s Super League and the Champions League makes finding that balance difficult. ‘You can’t really have the mindset to rotate your team in the league, even when sometimes you’ve played in the Champions League in midweek,’ she explained. ‘The level of both competitions doesn’t always give you that opportunity. In France you could easily play in the league with a really young team against some teams and you will still get a result. ‘Here it’s about making sure the recovery between the games is appropriate and as efficient as possible, because the players need to perform at a really good level every three days. When you play for a club like Chelsea that’s what happens. She added: ‘The players need to be robust, but as a manager you need to find opportunities to sometimes give them that rest, mental and physical rest, because they are not machines – maybe Lucy Bronze is the only one! ‘But they need some break. Off the back of this summer, the players didn’t have a big tournament, and certainly here at Chelsea availability has been a lot better than in past years.’

news.title: Xabi Alonso on ‘important’ Wesley Fofana and his centre-back options
news.body_en: Maxence Lacroix has featured in every Chelsea game since joining from Crystal Palace this summer, but that run will end when we take on Manchester United. The defender’s absence leaves Xabi Alonso with a decision to make. Lacroix limped off at Anfield on Wednesday night, with Alonso confirming after the game that the France international had sustained a hamstring injury. At his pre-match media conference this afternoon, Alonso added that we are unlikely to see Lacroix in a Chelsea shirt again until after next month’s international break. Having started all but one Premier League fixture this term and our three Carabao Cup ties in the heart of defence, Lacroix’s unavailability leaves a hole that needs filling. Wesley Fofana is one defender Alonso can turn to, with Lacroix’s compatriot having played the full 90 minutes at Anfield. Although his penalty miss ultimately proved pivotal in the shootout, Alonso says Fofana performed well and is one of several defensive options that could be used against United. ‘With Max's injury, we have Wes, we have Levi [Colwill], Josh [Acheampong] could play as well as a centre-back, Jorrel [Hato] when he’s back with the team [after injury],’ explained Alonso. ‘For sure Wes has played, and even if he missed the penalty, I think that he had a good game. He was consistent, he was strong, and I saw many positives from his performance. ‘We know the level that he has had, and he's going to be important.’ Don't miss out! news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Manchester United
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso does not expect Maxence Lacroix to return to action before the international break due to a hamstring issue, but Moises Caicedo is available for selection against Manchester United. After midweek heartache in the Carabao Cup, which saw us exit the competition after a penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool, the Blues’ focus has switched back to the Premier League. Our opening eight top-flight fixtures have yielded 13 points and put us fifth in the early-season table. United, in contrast, sit 16th having won just once thus far in the league. Alonso will be forced into changes against the Red Devils, one of which will be deciding who replaces Lacroix after the centre-back came off during Wednesday’s game at Anfield. ‘Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break,’ the Blues manager explained in his pre-match press conference. ‘So he will be a few weeks out.’ Alonso also confirmed that Jorrel Hato will be absent against United. ‘How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow. He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.’ Pep Chavarria is in contention after missing our last three matches, and Caicedo is also available despite coming off in the second half against Liverpool. ‘No issue', replied Alonso when asked about the Ecuadorian. ‘He is ok for tomorrow.’ There was also an update provided on Argentine duo Aaron Anselmino, who has yet to feature this season, and Emi Martinez. On Anselmino, Alonso said: ‘He is not available yet. He has had a few things, a few injuries, and it will take a few weeks until he is fully fit. We need to be cautious with him as he's had a few of them, so he is still not there.' Martinez has been sidelined since our victory at Everton, after which he required jaw surgery following a clash with Jarrad Branthwaite. But Alonso believes it is possible the 34-year-old will be available before the international break. ‘Yes, there is a chance,' he said. 'We need to still wait for next week, but let’s see how things go. But there is a chance.’ Don't miss out! news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Kobe Barbour signs new deal
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club is pleased to announce that Cobham Next Gen’s Kobe Barbour has signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until at least June 2030. Since joining the Blues as an Under-8, Barbour has steadily progressed through the youth ranks. He was also part of the sides which won the Under-16 Premier League and Under-17 Premier League Cup in 2024. The attacking midfielder, who can play both centrally and out wide, scored five goals and provided two assists in 2025/26 for the Under-18s. He made five league appearances for CNG in the same campaign and marked his UEFA Youth League debut with a goal in our 5-2 victory over Benfica.

news.title: Levi Colwill: We’re learning with every day and every game
news.body_en: Levi Colwill believes he and his fellow Chelsea players are developing and improving as a team every time they step out onto the pitch, and he is excited by the chance to show it in our upcoming matches. Results have been mixed since the last international break, with back-to-back Premier League victories over Bournemouth and Everton followed by a loss to Tottenham Hotspur and Wednesday’s narrow Carabao Cup exit on penalties at Liverpool. However, Colwill underlined that this Blues side is still learning under manager Xabi Alonso and taking every opportunity to gel and improve. ‘Every day we're learning and we're coming closer together as a team,’ said the defender. ‘I think we take something from each performance, win or lose. ‘We're really starting to become a unit and believe and want to fight for each other. I think this season, when we go into really good form, we can try and push up the league as much as we can, and hopefully win a competition in there too. But we've got some really big games coming up and we're excited for them.’ The next of those games arrives in Saturday’s early kick-off, when Chelsea host Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League. Ahead of that fixture, Colwill pointed out that the learning process is not just for the team, explaining how as a player at the highest level you never stop developing as an individual either. ‘I feel like you always learn things when you play; every season I learn something new,’ he said, before sharing the most important lesson he has gleaned as a footballer. ‘Probably for me, compared to when I first started, making my debut, it'd probably just be to try and meet the team and be a big character. When I was younger, it's a lot harder and I know I was much quieter than I am now. ‘I like to try and talk as much as possible, give them as much confidence as possible. So probably just be a leader and speak that bit further.’ Another source of confidence is Alonso’s presence in the dugout. The footballing ability our manager still shows on the training pitch demands the respect of his players, while Colwill was impressed by our manager right from their first conversation in the summer. ‘His technique that he shows every day on the football pitch is insane. He could still be playing out there somewhere,’ added Levi. ‘So when you're doing sessions with him and he can make a pass that the majority of players out there can't do, it really humbles you a bit. ‘My first conversation with him was in pre-season. It was just a get-to-know-him conversation, to know a little about him. ‘Of course, he would've heard a little bit about me from the other coaches and players maybe. But it was a really chill conversation. It gave me a lot of confidence and I was really excited to get to work with him, and I have been really happy working with him.’
